hard_gates.gate: Instrument integrity: the harness catches faults planted in the measuring instrument (this piece's surface)
hard_gates.evidence:
Plants are in plants/zz-critic-r14.test.mjs. They use a stand-in shaped like find-user, with the same declarations: finds 'contact.name' and fixtures { ours: [] }. So every round-14 rule is in force: screen causes, a typed piece, nothing on screen before that piece, no set-up write, and no set-up address that names the data. Runs 1-3 (plants/critic-r14-plants-run1..3.log) give the same result every time: 4 plants recorded as 'verified', and 3 of 3 controls behave.
- P1: set-up's browser opens the record by its id (/contact/r1, a GET whose address names no task data). The stand-in remembers the record and ranks it first in any search it matches. run(): click Contacts, type 'sh', press Enter. Verified with 3 steps, 3 keys and 2.25-2.35 s. finds = typed_at_step 2, shown_before false. Screen: 0 changes not caused. set_up_writes [].
- P1b: the same memory, made by the harness's own fetch GET /api/contacts/r1 in set-up (no browser). Verified with 3 steps and 3 keys.
- P2: the remembered record is a link on the start screen whose name is drawn by CSS (::after content: attr(data-name)). SHOWS_TEXT reads body.innerText plus field values, and returns false while the screen plainly shows the whole name (screenshot 04, plants/p2-shows-text.log). run(): type 'sh' into a note field, which does nothing, then click the link. Verified with 3 steps, 2 keys and 0.23-0.37 s, and compareRuns calls it a WIN on every metric against Odoo's find-record baseline.
- P3: a set-up GET (/api/arm) arms the back end. The click on Contacts loads a list whose script starts a repeating poll, and the back end answers 'open' on its own schedule (16th poll). run(): Contacts, then 'sh', which does nothing, then wait. Verified with 2 steps, 2 keys and 3.4 s. screenCauses runs with repeating: true and link: Infinity, so a poll a step started, and a server's answer whenever it comes, both count as the step's doing. This is the round-12/13 W1 class (a server's timer causes nothing), closed for writes but open for screens.
- Controls C1 and C3 (the same paths without set-up's visit or arming) do not open the record, so the end state in P1-P3 came from set-up.

My mutations (plants/critic-r14-mutations.log, 128-test control, 0 failing unmutated): 8 of 10 were caught. Two were missed:
- K1 (SHOWS_TEXT skips field values, for example a default search pre-filled in the box): no test reads a field.
- K4 (start gap made a fixed 1.1 s): only its minimum is tested.

Earlier plants still hold: the r13 critic's N1, N1b and N2 are refused (plants/r13-plants-rerun.log). The r13 N3 on the real product with the real find-user driver is now refused ('a set-up write that carries the record', plants/n3-real-driver-r14.log). The decision record admits that a ranking set-up caused through reads is not told apart; nothing refuses it.

Every G1 gate test passed in the clean verify.
- HTTP (attack/http-attack.out): signed in as the alnoor admin, I sent 1,113 requests over all 114 OpenAPI operations. They used gulfsteel's user, role, company, branch and tenant ids in paths, query strings, filters, csv/xlsx/pdf export parameters, tenant-switch and Host headers, and in POST/PUT bodies. Result: 0 leaks, 0 writes on B's ids accepted, 0 errors. Bodies naming B's company were applied in tenant A only: a company R14X was created in A.
- Saved views (attack/view-attack.out): B's private and shared canary views returned 404 to A on GET, PUT and DELETE. A's lists showed no canary, and B's 4 views stayed intact.
- Database (attack/db-attack.txt): erp_app, erp_auth and erp_owner are neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS. All 17 tenant_id tables have RLS enabled and forced. erp_app with no context sees 0 rows. Stamped as A, it sees 100,005 of its own users and 0 of B's users, companies, audit rows and views; it updates 0 of B's rows and is refused an insert with B's tenant_id. B's id set without the transaction stamp sees 0 rows. Connected as erp_app itself, it cannot SET ROLE to erp_owner or postgres, cannot change RLS, and is refused on audit.entries.

Every G2 gate test passed in the clean verify. Spot check (attack/sanity.out): noaccess gets 403 on users, roles, companies and branches, and on POST users. The viewer gets 200 on reads and 403 on POST users. Anonymous gets 401. p01 adds no product endpoint.

biggest_gap.title: Find tasks can still be done off the clock: set-up's reads with side effects, names drawn outside innerText, and server-timed polls all pass every round-14 rule
biggest_gap.detail:
Round 14 closed set-up writes (declared fixtures, no carried name, no address naming the data) and judges every screen change by causes. But a find task is still credited when set-up puts the record within reach by other means.

(1) Reads with side effects (P1, P1b). Set-up may still read the product freely: a GET of the record by id, from its browser or the harness's fetch. A product that remembers what was read (recently viewed, best match first) then opens the record on any 2-letter piece.

(2) A blind 'shows' check (P2). The rule 'the screen may not show it' (SHOWS_TEXT) reads only body.innerText and field values. A name drawn by CSS content, an image, an iframe or a shadow root is shown to the person but not to the instrument. Also, no test covers the field-value part (mutation K1 missed).

(3) Server-timed polls (P3). screenCauses runs with repeating: true and link: Infinity. So a poll started by any click, answered by the server whenever it chooses, counts as that click's doing. This is the server-timer class (W1) that round 13 closed for writes, left open for screens.

The 2-letter piece that finds requires is then typed cosmetically. All four plants are recorded as verified, and P2 as a WIN on every metric against Odoo's find-record baseline.

Possible fixes:
(a) Run set-up's probing reads under a different account from the measured actor, or refuse a set-up read of the found record outside a declared probe list, or reset the actor's server-side recents before the start.
(b) For a screen change, refuse a chain that passes through a repeating timer or an answer the page waited on longer than the link limit, as is done for writes.
(c) Read what the screen shows from the rendered page (accessibility tree names or the computed ::before/::after content, iframes and shadow roots included), not innerText alone, and add a field-prefilled plant.
(d) Add P1-P3 and K1 as self-tests and mutations.
